content:
Let \(\theta=\angle DAB\). Then area of \(ABCD\) is \(169\sin\theta\).

Since \(AF\parallel BD\) but points outside \(ABCD\), set \(\vec{AF}=-k\vec{BD}\) with \(k>0\). From \(|AF|=13\),
\[
k=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2-2\cos\theta}}.
\]
The area of rhombus \(BAFC\) is
\[
|\vec{AB}\times \vec{AF}|=169k\sin\theta=65.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{169\sin\theta}{\sqrt{2-2\cos\theta}}=65.
\]
Using \(\sqrt{2-2\cos\theta}=2\sin(\theta/2)\) and \(\sin\theta=2\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)\),
\[
169\cos(\theta/2)=65 \implies \cos(\theta/2)=\frac5{13}.
\]
So \(\sin(\theta/2)=\frac{12}{13}\), hence
\[
\sin\theta=2\cdot\frac5{13}\cdot\frac{12}{13}=\frac{120}{169}.
\]
Therefore the area of \(ABCD\) is
\[
169\cdot\frac{120}{169}=120.
\]

\[
\boxed{120}
\]
